ei.title: Waste, Demand, and Products as a Service
ei.subject: 10월_2025 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Waste, Demand, and Products as a Service

fullPassage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.

questions.passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be (A)[sustained / halted]. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is (B)[avoidable / inevitable], such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies (C)[abandon / maintain] profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) sustained=지속되는, (B) inevitable=불가피한, (C) maintain=유지하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① sustained — inevitable — maintain: 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② halted — inevitable — maintain: (A) halted(중단된)는 sustained(지속되는)의 반의어
❌ ③ sustained — avoidable — maintain: (B) avoidable(피할 수 있는)은 inevitable(불가피한)의 반의어
❌ ④ sustained — inevitable — abandon: (C) abandon(포기하다)은 maintain(유지하다)의 반의어
det.tip: demand will be sustained / waste is inevitable / maintain profit

questions.passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly (A)[independent / dependent] on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, (B)[limited / unlimited] access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are (C)[encouraged / discouraged] to develop long-lasting products.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) dependent=의존적인, (B) limited=제한된, (C) encouraged=격려받는/촉진되는
det.analysis:
❌ ① independent — limited — encouraged: (A) independent(독립적인)는 dependent(의존적인)의 반의어
❌ ② dependent — unlimited — encouraged: (B) unlimited(무제한의)는 limited(제한된)의 반의어
❌ ③ dependent — limited — discouraged: (C) discouraged(좌절된)는 encouraged(격려받는)의 반의어
✅ ④ dependent — limited — encouraged: 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: directly dependent / limited access / encouraged to develop

questions.passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. Many strategies have been (A)[excluded / incorporated] into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the (B)[elimination / preservation] of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this (C)[stagnation / transition] of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) incorporated=통합된/도입된, (B) elimination=제거, (C) transition=전환
det.analysis:
❌ ① excluded — elimination — transition: (A) excluded(배제된)는 incorporated(도입된)의 반의어
❌ ② incorporated — preservation — transition: (B) preservation(보존)은 elimination(제거)의 반의어
❌ ③ incorporated — elimination — stagnation: (C) stagnation(정체)은 transition(전환)의 반의어
✅ ④ incorporated — elimination — transition: 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: strategies have been incorporated / elimination of waste / transition of ownership

questions.passage: Waste has historically been seen as a ①<u>necessary</u> driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be ②<u>diminished</u>. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is ③<u>inevitable</u>, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a ④<u>replacement</u>. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '제품 수요가 지속될 것이다'라는 맥락. diminished(줄어든)는 sustained(지속되는)의 반의어
det.analysis:
❌ ① necessary — 원문 일치. '경제의 필수적인(necessary) 동력'에 적절
✅ ② diminished — 원문 sustained(지속되는). diminished(줄어든)로 바꾸면 '수요가 줄어들 것이다'로 글의 논리와 모순 ←정답
❌ ③ inevitable — 원문 일치. '낭비가 불가피한(inevitable) 것'에 적절
❌ ④ replacement — 원문 일치. '대체품(replacement)이 필요하다'에 적절
det.tip: demand will be sustained(지속되는) — 수요가 지속될 것이다

questions.passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be ①<u>wasted</u>, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '기업이 유지보수 서비스를 제공하여 이익을 유지한다'는 맥락. deficit(적자)은 profit(이익)의 반의어
det.analysis:
❌ ① wasted — 원문 일치. '제품이 낭비되도록(wasted) 디자인한다'에 적절
❌ ② cheap — 원문 일치. '저렴한(cheap) 재료 사용'에 적절
✅ ③ deficit — 원문 profit(이익). deficit(적자)으로 바꾸면 '적자를 유지한다'로 맥락과 모순 ←정답
❌ ④ long-lasting — 원문 일치. '오래 지속되는(long-lasting) 제품'에 적절
det.tip: maintain profit(이익을 유지하다) — 서비스를 통해 이익을 유지

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '내구성 있는 제품 개발이 촉진된다'는 맥락. compelled(강요받는)는 encouraged(격려받는)와 뉘앙스가 다름
det.analysis:
❌ ① driver — 원문 일치. '경제의 동력(driver)'에 적절

❌ ③ supported — 원문 일치. '낭비가 필요하다는 생각을 지지한(supported) 사람들'에 적절
✅ ④ compelled — 원문 encouraged(격려받는/촉진되는). compelled(강제된)로 바꾸면 '내구성 제품 개발을 강제당한다'로 자발적 동기부여 맥락과 모순 ←정답

det.korean: replacement=대체품 (소비자가 결국 대체품을 필요로 하게 된다)
det.analysis:

questions.passage:
(A) Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is <u>inevitable</u>.
(B) The traffic jam was <u>inevitable</u> given that three lanes were closed for construction.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 inevitable이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) inevitable=불가피하도록 의도된(전략적으로 낭비를 피할 수 없게 만듦), (B) inevitable=상황상 불가피한(공사로 인한 자연스러운 결과)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 우연한 — (B) 피할 수 없는: (A)에서 inevitable은 '전략적으로 보장된' 것이지 우연이 아님
❌ ② (A) 피할 수 없는 — (B) 당연한: 두 맥락의 뉘앙스 차이를 반영하지 못함
❌ ③ (A) 의도된 — (B) 자연스러운: '의도된'은 inevitable의 사전적 의미와 동떨어짐
✅ ④ (A) 불가피하도록 의도된 — (B) 상황상 불가피한: (A)는 전략적 의도, (B)는 외부 상황에 의한 불가피함 ←정답
det.tip: (A) ensure waste is inevitable = 낭비가 불가피하도록 보장 (의도적) vs (B) inevitable given that = ~을 감안하면 불가피한 (상황적)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the process of making a product that is no longer functional usable again by disassembling and rebuilding it"

det.korean: remanufacturing=재제조: 기능을 상실한 제품을 분해하고 다시 조립하여 사용 가능하게 만드는 과정
det.analysis:
✅ ① remanufacturing: remanufacturing(재제조)은 '분해하고 다시 조립'이라는 영영 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ② recycling: recycling(재활용)은 원재료 회수이지 제품 재조립이 아님
❌ ③ replacement: replacement(교체)는 새 제품으로 바꾸는 것
❌ ④ obsolescence: obsolescence(노후화)는 제품이 쓸모없어지는 과정
det.tip: remanufacturing = disassembling + rebuilding = 재제조

questions.passage: Many strategies have been __________ (incorporate) into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: incorporate → incorporated: 현재완료 수동(have been + 과거분사)
det.analysis: have been __________ (incorporate) — 현재완료 수동 구조(have been + p.p.). incorporated 필요
det.tip: have been incorporated — 현재완료 수동. 도입되어 왔다

questions.passage: Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that __________ (priority) the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: priority → prioritizing: 명사 → 동명사(동사 prioritize의 -ing형, 주어 역할)
det.analysis: that __________ (priority) the elimination — 주어 자리에 동명사가 필요. priority(명사)를 prioritize(동사)로 바꾸고 -ing 형태. creates의 주어이므로 동명사 prioritizing
det.tip: prioritizing the elimination — 제거를 우선시하는 것(동명사 주어)

questions.passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: __________. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 서비스로서의 제품 (수리와 재제조를 통한 새로운 수요 모델)
det.analysis:
❌ ① waste as a resource: 자원으로서의 낭비는 본문의 핵심 전환과 다른 개념
✅ ② products as a service: 원문 일치. 'creates a different kind of demand: products as a service' ←정답
❌ ③ demand as a challenge: 도전으로서의 수요는 본문에 언급 없음
❌ ④ profit as a priority: 우선순위로서의 이익은 서비스 모델 전환과 다른 방향
det.tip: a different kind of demand: products as a service — 서비스로서의 제품

Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 유지보수 및 수리 서비스 (기업이 소유권 전환 후 이익을 유지하는 방법)
det.analysis:
❌ ① advertising and promotion strategies: 광고·홍보 전략은 서비스 모델의 이익 원천이 아님
✅ ② maintenance and repair services: 원문 일치. 'maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services' ←정답
❌ ③ production and export operations: 생산·수출 운영은 서비스 모델이 아닌 제조 모델
❌ ④ research and innovation programs: 연구·혁신 프로그램은 이익 유지의 직접 수단이 아님
det.tip: maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services — 유지보수와 수리 서비스를 제공하여 이익을 유지
